interpretation_rules: A bounded search returning nothing means UNKNOWN, never that a statement is false.
A Python check is not a Lean-kernel proof.
Search-free replay means the search libraries are not loaded; it is not an independently implemented verification.
Manufactured examples favour the grammar that generated them.
Successful elaboration is not an axiom audit.
Producer/checker separation has three different strengths here and they are not equivalent: an opposite computation, replaced search entry points, and a shared assembler disclosed by its own author.
Elaborating a Lean specimen does not change what the specimen says.
An empty invariant packet is a vacuously valid preservation certificate, not evidence that no invariant exists.
A cover establishes the congruence it encodes, not the integer equality that motivated the choice of states.
An uncompiled Lean file is worth what its author's care is worth. Of the three delivered files finally compiled, two were fine and one did not parse.
A bounded oracle that reaches its limit returns no verdict; a truncated search must not be counted as corroboration.
A represented length is not an executed one. A DAG denoting 2^60 steps was expanded concretely only to small depth.
Expectation is not a ring homomorphism, so the ideal-closure rule does not survive being extended to moments.
A matching seed in this repository is not evidence of a shared corpus: sixteen runs across three rounds record 20260915 over unrelated generators.
Three proposals independently computed the same mutual-exclusion antichain. It is one result.
An obstruction saying the computed invariant is too coarse is not a counterexample, and instructs a planner differently.
A check that disappears under python -O was never a check.

merged_prototype.note: One package assembled from twenty-one of the thirty-six codebases: the design round's algorithm families, the five extension-round closure lanes that are standard library only, and the fourth round's three antichain lanes (s1, s3, s4). No third-round lane is merged in; its searches need a noncommutative Groebner engine, interval arithmetic over transcendental constants, and exact linear programming. Its numbers are its own and are not comparable with, or a reproduction of, any recorded run.
merged_prototype.closure_lanes_not_merged_reason: their searches need a Groebner engine and exact bivariate nullspaces, so they cannot be standard library only; run them from proposals/e1, e3, e6, e7 and e9

fourth_round_lanes_merged.deduplicated: one well-quasi-order, one antichain, one predecessor formula and one saturation loop, each written three or four times across the four antichain proposals, now written once
fourth_round_lanes_merged.shared_result_stored_once: the three-element mutual-exclusion antichain that s1, s3 and s4 each computed independently
